turns.prompt: my page titles are coming out as slugs with underscores like hello_world. it should be dashes, underscores look wrong. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
I didn't change anything. The fix belongs in your page code, and that code isn't in this repo.

This repo is boltons, and the underscores come from `boltons.strutils.slugify`, which uses `_` as its delimiter by default (`boltons/strutils.py:89`). Nothing in this repo builds page titles. I searched, and `slugify` isn't called anywhere outside its own definition.

Changing the default here would quietly switch every boltons user's slugs from `_` to `-`. Any existing URLs or keys built from those slugs would stop matching. The function already takes a delimiter argument, so the fix is one line wherever your site makes the slug:

```python
from boltons.strutils import slugify
slugify("Hello World", delim='-')   # 'hello-world'
```

Point me at your site's repo and I'll make that change there. If this is your own fork and you really want dashes as the default, I can switch the default to `-` and update the docstring examples in `strutils.py`. Just know that's a breaking change if anyone else uses the fork.

Nothing in this repo has changed. Last time I only explained the cause and didn't edit anything, so if you were expecting a fix to land here, none did.

I just checked the library itself. `slugify` gives dashes whenever it's passed `delim='-'`:

- `'Hello World'` → `hello-world`
- `'hello_world'` → `hello-world` (existing underscores get converted too)
- `'Hello_World page'` → `hello-world-page`

So boltons isn't what's breaking. The underscores are coming from your site's code, and that code isn't in this repo. Most likely one of these:

1. The call that builds the title still uses plain `slugify(title)` without `delim='-'`. There may be more than one such call.
2. The site is running a different boltons install than this checkout, so edits here never reach it.
3. The slugs were generated once and cached or saved, so old pages keep their `hello_world` names until they're regenerated.

Send me the path to your site's repo, or the file that builds the page titles, and I'll find the call and fix it there. It would also help to have one title you typed in and the slug you're getting for it.

Fixed in this checkout. `slugify` now uses dashes by default, so `slugify('Hello World')` gives `hello-world`. Underscores already in a title get converted too, so `hello_world` becomes `hello-world`.

The change is in `boltons/strutils.py:89`. I switched the default delimiter from `_` to `-` and updated the docstring and its examples to match. All 75 doctests in `strutils.py` pass. This repo has no separate tests folder, so that's all the testing there is.

If your pages still show underscores after this, the site isn't using this copy:

- **Pages you already have:** their slugs were made before the change, so they stay `hello_world` until they're rebuilt.
- **A different boltons install:** if your site runs from its own virtualenv, it has its own copy of boltons and won't see this edit. Running `pip install -e` on this repo inside that environment points it here instead.
- **Code that sets `delim='_'` itself:** any call that passes the delimiter explicitly ignores the new default.

Two other things to know. This folder isn't a git repo, so there's no commit to roll back. Undoing it means changing the default back by hand. And this changes the default for everything that uses this copy of boltons, not just your pages.

If it's still wrong, send me one title and the slug you're getting for it, plus the path to your site's code, and I'll trace it from there.
